images.concept: Isometric infographic showing the 5-step feed-calculation workflow: pond → sampling 30 fish → Biomass × Feeding Rate formula → daily feed kg → 30 kg sack stack. Language-neutral icons, bilingual reuse.
images.prompt: Clean modern flat isometric infographic illustration showing the workflow for calculating tilapia feed requirements in aquaculture, arranged left-to-right in 5 connected steps: (1) a small isometric blue tarpaulin pond with a few tilapia fish silhouettes; (2) a curved arrow labeled with a sampling-net icon pointing to a small group of 30 fish on a hanging scale; (3) a clean rectangular formula box containing a stylized multiplication symbol between a 'Biomass' weight-scale icon and a 'Feeding Rate' percent-sign icon; (4) a calendar-day icon with a small bag-of-feed pictogram indicating daily feed in kilograms; (5) a stack of three 30-kilogram feed sacks. Connecting arrows between each step. Aquaculture color palette of soft blue, fresh aqua-green, and warm cream background. Subtle drop shadows. Iconographic and language-neutral so the same image works in Indonesian and English articles. Mobile-readable composition, 16:9 aspect ratio, professional aquaculture trade publication style. No text overlays, no numbers, no letters, no labels, no watermarks, no logos, no signatures.
images.alt_id: Diagram alur kalkulasi pakan ikan nila: kolam, sampling, rumus biomassa, pakan harian, sak 30 kg
images.alt_en: Tilapia feed calculation flow: pond, biomass sampling, formula box, daily feed, 30 kg sack stack
images.caption_id: Lima langkah inti kalkulasi pakan ikan nila per 1000 ekor: sampling biomassa, rumus biomassa kali feeding rate, pakan harian, dan konversi ke sak 30 kg. Total siklus khas: ~258 kg atau setara 9 sak.
images.caption_en: The five-step workflow for calculating tilapia feed requirements per 1,000 fish: biomass sampling, the biomass-times-feeding-rate formula, daily feed output, and conversion to 30 kg sacks — a typical cycle totals around 258 kg or 9 sacks.

images.concept: Editorial documentary photograph of an Indonesian smallholder farmer weighing a netted sample of tilapia on a hanging scale at the edge of a blue tarpaulin pond, golden-hour lighting, authentic field-work mood.
images.prompt: Editorial documentary photograph of an Indonesian smallholder tilapia farmer in his 40s, wearing a simple plain navy long-sleeve shirt and dark trousers (no visible brand logos or text on clothing), standing at the edge of a circular blue tarpaulin-lined intensive aquaculture pond in rural Indonesia. He is concentrated on weighing a small dip-net containing several live small-to-medium tilapia fish (Oreochromis niloticus) on a simple analog hanging spring scale held up at chest height. Water surface visible in pond with subtle ripples reflecting warm sky. Background softly out of focus shows rural Indonesian setting with green vegetation and a hint of bamboo or simple wooden structure. Golden hour late-afternoon sunlight bathes the scene with warm orange-amber tones, long soft shadows, gentle rim-lighting on the farmer's face and the dripping wet net of fish. Shot on a full-frame camera, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, sharp focus on the farmer's hands gripping the scale and the cluster of silver-grey tilapia in the net, photorealistic detail with accurate fish anatomy (correct number of fins, eyes, scales), natural skin tones, authentic working-farmer atmosphere not staged or commercial. Professional aquaculture trade publication style, 16:9 aspect ratio. No text overlays, no watermarks, no logos, no brand labels, no signatures, no AI stamps.
images.alt_id: Pembudidaya Indonesia menimbang sampel ikan nila di jala dengan timbangan gantung di tepi kolam terpal
images.alt_en: Indonesian smallholder farmer weighing a netted tilapia sample on a hanging scale at a tarpaulin pond edge
images.caption_id: Sampling bobot setiap 1 sampai 2 minggu adalah disiplin lapangan yang membuat hitungan pakan tetap akurat. Jala 30 sampai 50 ekor ditimbang massal, dibagi jumlah ekor, untuk dapat Mean Body Weight terkini.
images.caption_en: Sampling biomass every one to two weeks is the field discipline that keeps the feed calculation honest. A net of 30 to 50 fish is weighed collectively, then divided by the count, to update Mean Body Weight.
images.fallback_note: Editor should spot-check the rendered fish anatomy and scale-reading pose at full size — gpt-image-1 occasionally misrenders fish gill placement or scale dial details. If anatomy looks off, a stock photo (Shutterstock 'Indonesian fish farmer weighing tilapia') is a reliable swap.
